title: Read archaic wording in a natural voice
statement: Have the voice read archaic wording for meaning in its natural voice, with no put-on period accent, and guide its pronunciation without respelling the printed quotation.
detail: A lesson on a verse play sets its audio check as no forced fake Elizabethan accent, reading for meaning first while keeping the language, and says that a phonetic pronunciation aid is not a rewritten quotation. When the archaic thee was first transcribed as the and ere long as yearlong, the repairs gave the voice notes such as that ere rhymes with air and thee with see, while every printed word and grammatical ending stayed exact.
against: Human acceptance of the pronunciation is still open: "Human adult Grade 5 voice and literary-name/dialect pronunciation review" (grade3-reading/visual-findings-2026-09-07/review-readiness/curriculum-alignment/rebuild/media/FINAL-HANDOFF.json, line 28)

evidence.quote: Audio check: no forced fake Elizabethan accent. Read meaning first, preserving the language. A phonetic pronunciation aid is not a rewritten quotation.
Keep every word and grammatical ending exact. Build ends in a voiced d sound. The archaic ere rhymes with air. The archaic thee rhymes with see.
